numberToKorean.integerOnly: Amount notation supports positive whole numbers only
numberToKorean.title: Number to Korean
numberToKorean.description: Convert numeric and Korean amounts to Korean, formal Hanja, English, and mixed formats. Preserve editing position and recover failed single or batch copies with manual selection and retry.

usage.title: Use Cases
items: Compare written amounts and digits while preparing documents or receipts
Choose prefixes and compare formal Hanja and other output formats
Check how amounts containing Korean text are interpreted
Copy tables or download CSV for up to 100 input lines

rules.title: Korean Amount Notation Rules
items: Reading-oriented Korean and written-amount outputs use different omission rules. Choose the output you need.
Choose a Geum or Ilgeum prefix, no prefix, and spacing.
Formal Hanja, English, and mixed numeric formats are available; choose the format needed by your document.
Korean reading spells fractional digits after the decimal point. This differs from written-amount outputs intended for positive integers.

whatIs.title: What is the Number-to-Korean Converter?
whatIs.description: Convert numbers or amounts containing Korean text into several written formats while inspecting the current input and result. Editing does not forcibly reformat digits; explicit copying, batch conversion, and CSV export are available.

howToUse.title: How to Use
items: 1. Enter numbers or a Korean amount. Raw input and cursor position are preserved while editing; valid numeric input is tidied after editing.
2. Inspect Korean, Hanja, English, and mixed results and choose prefix and spacing options.
3. Copy the result you need. If it fails, select the complete text manually or retry the current result.
4. For multiple amounts, enter up to 100 lines in batch input and use the result table or CSV.

tips.title: Pro Tips
items: Check restored shared input before using an example or quick-amount button.
Numeric strings support up to 20 integer digits. Korean reverse conversion has a separate large-value limit.
Compare numeric and written amounts in the document and select the output format you need.

items.q: Why are commas not inserted immediately while editing?
items.a: Forced formatting is deferred to preserve insertion, deletion, IME composition, and cursor position. Valid numeric input is tidied after editing; Korean reverse-conversion text stays intact.
Numeric strings support up to 20 integer digits. Reverse conversion containing Korean keeps the existing safe-integer limit, so the limits are not interchangeable.
Korean, formal Hanja, English, mixed numeric outputs, and Korean reverse conversion are available. Some result formats depend on whether the input is fractional, negative, or a positive integer.

numberToKorean.copyFailed: Could not copy. Check your browser's clipboard permission or select and copy the result manually.

batch.title: Convert multiple amounts
batch.description: Enter one amount per line, or paste two spreadsheet columns: an item name and an amount. Use a tab between columns. Commas within amounts are preserved.
batch.options: Uses the settings above. Prefix: {prefix} · Unit spacing: {spacing}
batch.limits: Up to {lines} lines including blank lines, {characters} characters in total, and {lineCharacters} characters per line.
batch.privacy: This list is processed only on this screen. It is not saved to a server, shared URL, or browser storage. Refreshing clears the list.
batch.summary: {total} lines · {valid} converted · {invalid} errors · {skipped} blank lines skipped
batch.formalHint: {count} rows cannot use contract format: zero, negative, and fractional values only receive a Korean reading.
batch.blankHint: Blank lines are omitted from results while original line numbers are retained. Exceeding an overall limit stops output until you edit the input; it never produces a partial conversion.
batch.copied: Copied the entire table, including error rows.
batch.copyFailed: Could not copy the table. Check clipboard permission or download the CSV instead.
batch.downloadFailed: Could not prepare the file. Try again or copy the entire table.
batch.exportHint: Copied and downloaded tables include error rows in their original order. Converted fields remain empty for those rows, with the reason in the status column.
batch.spreadsheetHint: Item, source, and normalized number cells start with an apostrophe (') to protect them as text. Set those columns to Text when importing CSV too. Automatic numeric conversion may change amounts longer than 15 digits; some programs may display the protective apostrophe.
batch.formalUnavailable: No contract format · reading only for zero, negative, or fractional values

errors.tooManyCharacters: The total input limit is 30,000 characters. Your text has not been truncated. Shorten the input to resume conversion.
errors.tooManyLines: The limit is 100 lines including blanks. Your text has not been truncated. Remove some lines to resume conversion.
errors.lineTooLong: Each line may contain up to 300 characters.
errors.tooManyColumns: This line has three or more tab-separated columns. Provide only an item name and an amount.
errors.invalidAmount: Could not read the amount. Check the number format and the 20-digit limit for its integer part.

editing.example: This result uses the example amount 123,456,789 won. Replace it with your own number.
editing.blurHint: Your text is kept while you type. Numeric input gets grouping commas after you leave the field; Korean amount text is kept as entered.
editing.composing: Finish composing the text to use quick amounts and copy actions.

copyRecovery.failed: Could not finish copying {label}. Select the full text below or try again.
copyRecovery.hint: Select all, then use your device's copy command. Selecting text alone does not copy it to the clipboard.
copyRecovery.selectionFailed: The text could not be selected automatically. Select it directly in the text area.
